pr.title: Build a 64-bit Windows setup with Inno Setup 7
pr.body:
Refs #339236

On Windows on Arm, the VS Code installer takes much longer than it needs to because the setup is an x86 executable, and x86 emulation there is much slower than x64 emulation. Inno Setup 7 can build a 64-bit setup through the new [`SetupArchitecture`](https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/index.php?topic=setup_setuparchitecture) directive, but it still builds an x86 setup by default.

This PR sets `SetupArchitecture=x64` in `code.iss`. VS Code only ships x64 and arm64 builds, and both can run an x64 setup, so no per-arch condition is needed.

### Why the version guard

VS Code gets ISCC from the [`innosetup`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/innosetup) npm package ([joaomoreno/node-innosetup-compiler](https://github.com/joaomoreno/node-innosetup-compiler)). It's currently at **6.4.1**, which is also the latest version published to npm. Inno Setup 6 doesn't know the directive and would fail the build, so it's wrapped in `#if Ver >= EncodeVer(7, 0, 0)`. That makes this PR safe to merge now. It changes nothing until `innosetup` is updated to 7.x, and then it takes effect without further changes. Git for Windows used the same approach in https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/pull/732.

### 64-bit safety of the Pascal Script

Git for Windows had to fix record layouts for Windows API calls when moving to a 64-bit setup, because pointers become 8 bytes wide. `code.iss` doesn't declare any records. Its only external import is `MultiByteToWideChar`, whose parameters are all either 32-bit integers or string types that Pascal Script passes as pointers, so it is ABI-correct on x64 without changes. The script also uses none of the features that Inno Setup 7 removed for 64-bit setups (`{sysnative}`, `EnableFsRedirection`, or loading 32-bit DLLs).

### Testing

I compiled the full `code.iss` with the same `/d` definitions that `gulpfile.vscode.win32.ts` passes (quality `stable`, so the Appx code paths are included) against a stub source directory. I checked the PE machine type of each resulting `VSCodeSetup.exe`:

| Compiler | arm64 user | arm64 system | x64 user | x64 system |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inno Setup 6.4.1 (current `innosetup` npm) | x86 | x86 | x86 | x86 |
| Inno Setup 7.1.0 | **x64** | **x64** | **x64** | **x64** |

All builds succeed. The only new compiler warnings with 7.1.0 are about obsolete `[LangOptions]` font directives in one of the bundled `i18n/Default.*.isl` files, and they don't relate to this change.

I haven't run these stub setups end to end (installing or updating), since that needs a real build. That's worth doing on the first Inno Setup 7 build, including an update from an existing 32-bit-setup install, which Inno Setup documents as supported.

### Follow-up needed

Publish `innosetup@7.x` and bump `package.json`/`package-lock.json`. That step activates this change.

commit.message:
Build a 64-bit Windows setup with Inno Setup 7

Inno Setup 7 adds the SetupArchitecture directive but keeps building a
32-bit x86 setup by default. On Windows on Arm, x86 runs under much
slower emulation than x64, so the arm64 installer takes far longer than
it needs to.

Set SetupArchitecture=x64. VS Code only ships x64 and arm64 builds, both
of which can run an x64 setup. The directive doesn't exist in Inno Setup
6, which is what the innosetup npm package currently provides, so guard
it on the compiler version. The change takes effect as soon as that
dependency moves to 7.x.

Refs #339236
